title: Redwood Aug 2026 All-Hands — Leadership Update
summary: CEO opens with Q2 recap and positioning; product and infra lead highlight performance wins and Dedicated/Private milestones; sales covers pipeline and expansion; security update on SOC2 and private deployment readiness; PeopleOps shares hiring plan; Q3 OKRs and actions called out with owners.

Carlos Rivera - AE pricing deck update - 2026-08-18
transcript:
Header: Aug 12, 2026 10:00am PDT — Duration: 55 minutes — Attendees: ~220 on Zoom; leaders on stage listed below

[00:00] Elena Park: Hey, good morning everyone, thanks for joining. Quick housekeeping — recording is on, please keep questions to q&a at the end, we'll try to get through leadership updates then open floor. Excited to kick off.

[00:22] Elena Park: Quick high level — Q2 was a good quarter, we beat our revenue plan by about 8%, pipeline is strong, durable adoption in mid-market, couple of nice Dedicated renewals. Not everything perfect, we had a few incidents in late June that impacted some customers, Tom will cover remediation.

[01:05] Marcus Lee: Hi all — engineering update. We rolled out the continuous batching improvements across hosted last month; median latency for 512-token workloads is down ~18% on our verified models, and p95 down closer to 22%. There's still tail work for heterogeneous hardware but overall throughput improved, and cost per token moved down about 10% in our test clusters. Note: some of the numbers in the slides were from an early run, sorry if slides show slightly different, I'll post corrected benchmarks.

[02:12] Priya Shah: Product — we shipped function-calling GA for a subset of customers, improved streaming stability, and added structured output templates. On roadmap: Dedicated autoscaling improvements, Private deployment installer (beta for 3 customers), and Optimize recommendations UI. We'll open public roadmap v2 next week.

[03:10] Carlos Rivera: Sales — pipeline healthy. Big focus on a few mid-market accounts that are close to conversion, also renewals for two large Dedicated customers in September. We're seeing more procurement questions around data residency and SOC2, security docs are a gating factor for larger deals. Also pricing sensitivity on high-throughput use cases, so Optimize features matter.

[04:00] Jenna Kim: Research — model onboarding: we validated two new open LLMs for the catalog with better perf on quantized paths; results look promising though some safety regressions to be addressed. We'll be putting together evaluation sets for those models and share with product and AE teams.

[04:45] Tom Nguyen: Infra update — incident recap: late June we had a cascading autoscaler bug that caused spikes and degraded some Dedicated pools. Root cause was a mis-specified threshold in the autoscaler; we've rolled a fix, added additional alarms and a canary rollout for autoscale changes. Also we're progressing on private on-prem installer and VPC networking docs. For customers doing private deployments, the KMS/HSM integration testing is ongoing with one partner.

[06:10] Elena Park: On SOC2 — security team is on track, we're estimating final report Q3 end; that will remove a major procurement blocker. Also, we're accelerating the Private product for regulated customers. Important for marketing and sales to update collateral once SOC2 is in place.

[07:05] Marcus Lee: Quick note on performance engineering: KV cache improvements shipped last week, some transcriptions in the slides may say "KV cash" which is a transcription bug, but it reduced repeat-token cost in our caches by about 12% in internal tests. I'm going to share the full runbook and detailed numbers.

[08:00] Audience question (chat): Is there a formal SLA for dedicated? Carlos: Yes, we offer SLA on Dedicated for customers with contracts; specifics vary by tier, we'll get legal to standardize language and publish a short FAQ.

[09:05] Priya Shah: On roadmap prioritization — Q3 focus: 1) Dedicated reliability and canary rollouts, 2) Private deployment UX, 3) Optimize recommendations accuracy and UI, 4) Improved billing/usage analytics. We're tracking these as primary OKRs.

[10:12] Elena Park: Hiring — we are pausing a couple of junior IC reqs to prioritize senior infra and product hires. People Ops will publish the hiring prioritization doc. We need good interviewers across engineering and product, please volunteer.

[11:05] Carlos Rivera: A note on go-to-market — PLG motion still core, but we're leaning into sales-assisted deals for Dedicated & Private. We closed one strategic partner this quarter which gives us better APAC presence. Also worth flagging competition from big cloud providers tying their endpoints to infra, we need to emphasize our cost controls and unified runtime story.

[12:30] Jenna Kim: On model quality monitoring — we've added prompt-set regression alerts in-stage, early signals are good but we need to scale to more customers. Quality alerts will be tied to Optimize recommendations.

[13:20] Tom Nguyen: For Private customers — network docs and the on-prem installer mean less manual ops; we expect two pilot installs in August. There may be some timeline slippage depending on partner testing.

[14:00] Internal comment (quiet): someone says "great work team" in chat.

[15:10] Elena Park: Strategy recap — position Redwood as production-first inference with predictable economics and unified runtime. The competitive differentiator is that we balance cost controls with reliability and private options; keep using that language in comms.

[16:00] Q&A open:
[16:05] Question from Engineering (voice): Are there plans to open-source any of the runtime kernel selection? Marcus: Short answer no for now, we might publish some research notes but not the production code.

[18:30] Question from Sales: Any change to pricing approach for high-throughput customers? Carlos: We're updating the AE playbook and will include bundled offers for Dedicated capacity and committed burst credits; pricing deck will be sent.

[20:10] Question from Security: SOC2 gap list — Maya from security: We pushed remediation tasks, some vendor controls pending, expect closure by next month.

[22:00] Interruptions/crosstalk during a mic test, audio glitch for ~30s; apologies.

[22:40] Priya Shah: Demo note — we removed a flaky demo from the public deck; new demo uses a smaller prompt set for reliability. If you reuse demo assets, pull the latest from /docs/demo.

[24:00] Carlos Rivera: A quick shoutout to AE Sarah for landing a tricky renewal, and to infra on the autoscale fix.

[25:00] Elena Park: Ok, closing notes — Q3 is about shipping reliability and enabling enterprise readiness. Keep customer obsession, and escalate blockers early. We'll hold an all-hands follow-up office hours next Wednesday to dig into team-specific questions.

[25:40] Closing: Elena thanks everyone, sign off.

Notes: Transcript has occasional mis-recognitions (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, "function calling GA" spoken fast), timestamps approximate. Slides referenced: Q2 results deck (link in calendar invite), SOC2 gap doc (internal link), benchmark spreadsheet (will be posted by Marcus).
